Cytology or histopathology must confirm high-grade / large-cell gastrointestinal lymphoma confined to the abdomen. No previous chemotherapy; FeLV/FIV-negative and suitable for anesthesia. Investigator screening includes blood count, chemistry, urinalysis, chest radiographs and abdominal ultrasound. Visits in Columbia, Missouri weekly for at least eight weeks, then every three weeks for five more visits.

Dogs must be at least 12 months old with a confirmed eligible cancer. No previous corticosteroids, chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiation. The study team screens for conditions that could interfere with treatment and excludes dogs with procedures under general anesthesia planned during the study.

A bladder/urethral mass strongly suspicious for invasive urothelial carcinoma may enter screening; cystoscopy confirms diagnosis before treatment. All arms include vinblastine, deracoxib and cPD-L1 immunotherapy. Creatinine must be at most 2.0 mg/dl; previous chemotherapy/radiation are excluded. NSAIDs require a 5–14-day washout; supplements require two weeks off, and current Librela/Cytopoint are not allowed.
